points.description: States that a higher priority process/task is blocked, delayed or unable to get the CPU (or run).
points.partial_credit: Half if only vaguely stated (e.g. 'priorities get mixed up' or 'a process is delayed') without naming the higher priority process being blocked.

points.description: States that this happens because a lower priority process holds a resource (e.g. lock/semaphore/mutex) that the higher priority process needs, so the lower priority one effectively runs ahead.
points.partial_credit: Half if the lower priority process is mentioned as the cause but the held resource is not mentioned, or the resource is mentioned vaguely.

rubric.notes: Full marks (2) need both ideas: a higher priority process cannot run/get CPU, and the cause is a lower priority process holding a needed resource. Give 1 mark if only one idea is clear or both are stated vaguely. Give 0 for wrong or unrelated definitions, such as plain starvation or deadlock with no lower-priority-holds-resource idea. Different wording and synonyms (task, thread, lock) are fine.
